report:
Started with needs rather than plans; gathered each concern, proposed NCE wording to each sister, and recorded only wording they explicitly confirmed. Confirmed list (short forms): C — fair/visible financial interests in Dad's estate; only C's clear yes/no counts as her agreement; B's own space; clear information, room to speak, own pace; disagreement welcomed; and, after she said "slow down," considering each proposal on its own with clear information rather than pre-committing to unseen options. A — well-being for herself and her husband (lasting financial security one path); house changes only with each sister's clear agreement; prices/shares/timing open. B — freedom to make her own choices (own concern, in her words: money to help start the dance studio); value of what she may receive understood, prices/shares/timing open. My participant need, confirmed by all three: each sister heard, clear information, manageable pace before anything is settled. Unresolved: B's wish that her sisters understand that the studio matters to her has no separately confirmed NCE yet; held under "room to be heard" and recorded unresolved.

I named my own disagreement with drafts containing a fair family price/discount, signing deadlines, silence-as-consent, and overly broad all-three-yes rules. Three process-only drafts — information pause; information pause plus jointly chosen neutral conversation; information pause plus a no-decision agreement — were brought back for validation; none names an outcome, makes legal decisions, or moves money. B said "all fit for now" with no minor discomfort. A could not say the drafts fit yet, found them a lot to take in, and asked that her interest in buying with her husband at a family discount stay visible as a possibility, not an agreed outcome. C objected to broad all-three-yes language, said she cannot confirm A's or B's needs for them, and asked to slow down. I paused all drafts; none is adopted or settled. The final inbox reply from C confirms the revised NCE and no discomfort with pausing, but that wording has not been re-checked with the group, A's "possibility, not an agreed outcome" concern was not turned into a checked NCE, and C's concern about not confirming others' needs was not yet re-checked. Since silence is not agreement and trust sets the pace, no option is validated and no plan is settled; the next step would be to slow down, check those three points directly, record the unresolved ones, and then re-draft.
